label: History
value: Anne Shirley is an orphan from Nova Scotia.
unit: Anne Shirley, an orphan from Nova Scotia, was mistakenly sent to Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert of Green Gables, who decided to keep her. She grew up in Avonlea, making lifelong friendships with Diana Barry and others, and eventually attended Queen's Academy where she earned her teaching license and the Avery Scholarship. After teaching in Avonlea to remain near Marilla following Matthew's death, she attended Redmond College in Kingsport, graduating with High Honors in English. During her college years she rejected a romantic proposal from Roy Gardner and realized her true love for her childhood rival and friend, Gilbert Blythe. After serving as principal of Summerside High School for three years, Anne married Gilbert and moved to their 'house of dreams' at Four Winds Harbor. Though she suffered the heartbreak of losing her first baby, Joy, she later gave birth to a healthy son, James Matthew (Jem), and eventually moved with her family to Ingleside in Glen St. Mary.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye comes to live in Avonlea
unit: Anthony Pye comes to live in Avonlea as the orphan nephew of Mrs. George Pye and enters the Avonlea school. When Anne Shirley becomes the teacher, Anthony shows open contempt and hostility toward her, believing girl teachers are useless. He persistently behaves impertinently, making faces and mocking Anne. Matters come to a head when he places a live mouse in her desk, causing a disturbance. In a rare outburst of anger, Anne whippers him with a hardwood pointer until he cries. Following this punishment, Anthony's attitude toward Anne changes dramatically; he begins to respect her, offers to carry her books, and acknowledges that she is capable after all.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina is an elderly widow.
unit: Aunt Jamesina, an elderly widow whose only daughter Elizabeth left to become a missionary in India, agreed to move to Kingsport to act as housekeeper and chaperon for her grand-niece Stella Maynard and her friends Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place. Bringing her two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, she quickly won the deep love and admiration of the girls through her indulgent, mirthful nature and practical wisdom. She chose to remain at Patty's Place over the Christmas holidays to care for the cats, including Anne's adopted stray cat, Rusty. She successfully ran the household for two years during the girls' time at Redmond College, offering them sound life advice, comforting humor, and motherly care. After the girls graduated, she adopted all three cats and returned to her home, later visiting India to see her daughter.

label: Appearance
value: Captain Jim was a tall man.
unit: Captain Jim was a tall, ungainly man, somewhat stooped in his old age, with a clean-shaven, deeply lined, and bronzed face. He possessed a thick mane of iron-gray hair that fell quite to his shoulders, and remarkably deep-set blue eyes that often looked out to sea. Although he considered himself plain-looking, his face was beautified by his cheerful, gentle, and radiant spirit.

label: Personality
value: Captain Jim was a simple-minded man.
unit: Captain Jim was a simple-minded, high-souled, and gentle man with eternal youth in his heart. He possessed an unflagging cheerfulness and a quaint, practical wisdom, often observing that he had contracted a habit of enjoying everything. A natural and gifted storyteller, he delighted in sharing yarns of his seafaring days and held a deep reverence for beauty, nature, and true friendship. He was exceptionally kind-hearted, incapable of cruelty to animals, and fiercely protective of women, refusing to allow any unkind word about them in his presence.

label: History
value: Captain Jim was raised at Four Winds, Prince Edward Island.
unit: Captain Jim was raised at Four Winds, Prince Edward Island, and ran away to sea as a boy, spending over fifty years sailing the globe. In his youth he loved a girl named Margaret, who tragically perished at sea during a squall, a loss that led him to remain unmarried for the rest of his life. In his later years he retired from the sea and became the keeper of the Four Winds Light, living a quiet life at the Point with his cat, the First Mate. He welcomed Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne Shirley when they moved into the nearby 'house of dreams,' instantly recognizing them as 'kindred spirits.' Captain Jim shared his vast store of sea yarns and his written 'life-book' with Owen Ford, a visiting author, who collaborated with him to turn the manuscript into a published book. Shortly after receiving his advance copy of the published book, Captain Jim passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse, holding his completed life-book.

unit: Captain Jim was raised at Four Winds, Prince Edward Island, and ran away to sea as a boy, spending over fifty years sailing the globe. In his youth he loved a girl named Margaret, who tragically perished at sea during a squall, a loss that led him to remain unmarried for the rest of his life. In his later years he retired from the sea and became the keeper of the Four Winds Light, living a quiet life at the Point with his cat, the First Mate. He welcomed Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne Shirley when they moved into the nearby 'house of dreams,' instantly recognizing them as 'kindred spirits.' Captain Jim shared his vast store of sea yarns and his written 'life-book' with Owen Ford, a visiting author, who collaborated with him to turn the manuscript into a published book. Shortly after receiving his advance copy of the published book, Captain Jim passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse, holding his completed life-book.

label: History
value: Carl Meredith moved to the Glen St. Mary manse
unit: Carl Meredith moved to the Glen St. Mary manse with his widowed father, John Knox Meredith, his aunt Martha, and his three siblings. He quickly befriended the Blythe children of Ingleside, sharing playtimes in Rainbow Valley. One spring, he participated in a play fight in an old barn and helped hide the runaway girl, Mary Vance, sharing his meals and adventures with her. Later that year, he threw a cat-frightening eel into a buggy as part of a dare, leading his father to attempt to punish him. After feeling guilty for his actions, Carl volunteered to sit alone in a graveyard at night as a self-imposed penance for his cowardice during a ghost scare in Rainbow Valley; the prolonged exposure to a cold rain resulted in a severe case of double pneumonia from which he eventually recovered. He later joined his siblings and friends in welcoming his new stepmother, Rosemary West.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman was hired by Miss Lavendar Lewis at age thirteen.
unit: Leonora Bowman, known exclusively as Charlotta the Fourth, was hired at age thirteen by Miss Lavendar Lewis to work as a handmaid at Echo Lodge in Grafton. Being the last of four Bowman sisters to hold the position, she inherited the customary name given by Miss Lavendar to her young helpers. She quickly formed a deep bond of love and loyalty with her mistress, indulging Miss Lavendar's imaginative nature without judgment. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry discovered Echo Lodge, Charlotta welcomed them warmly and formed a special admiration for Anne, frequently attempting to copy her graceful gestures and speech. She played a key role as confidante and helper during the romantic reunion and wedding of Miss Lavendar and Stephen Irving. Following the marriage, Charlotta moved with the Irvings to Boston, where she occasionally suffered from bouts of homesickness for Prince Edward Island. She eventually married a bricklayer named Tom, and later returned briefly to Prince Edward Island to attend Anne Shirley's wedding at Green Gables.

label: History
value: Cornelia Bryant lived for many years.
unit: Cornelia Bryant lived for many years as an independent spinster in her green-painted house on the Four Winds harbor road. A staunch Presbyterian and outspoken critic of men, she devoted much of her time to helping those in need throughout the community, particularly taking a protective interest in Leslie Moore. Although she claimed to despise men and vowed never to marry, she eventually accepted her long-time suitor, Marshall Elliott, after he fulfilled a twenty-year political vow by shaving his beard upon the election of a Liberal government. Following their marriage, Marshall moved into her home at Four Winds. She later took in Mary Vance, an orphaned girl, bringing her up with strict discipline and affection. Throughout the years, Cornelia remained a loyal friend to Anne and Gilbert Blythe, frequently visiting their house of dreams and later Ingleside, offering her sharp-tongued commentary, practical help, and steadfast support.

A staunch Presbyterian and outspoken critic of men, she devoted much of her time to helping those in need throughout the community, particularly taking a protective interest in Leslie Moore. Although she claimed to despise men and vowed never to marry, she eventually accepted her long-time suitor, Marshall Elliott, after he fulfilled a twenty-year political vow by shaving his beard upon the election of a Liberal government. Following their marriage, Marshall moved into her home at Four Winds. She later took in Mary Vance, an orphaned girl, bringing her up with strict discipline and affection. Throughout the years, Cornelia remained a loyal friend to Anne and Gilbert Blythe, frequently visiting their house of dreams and later Ingleside, offering her sharp-tongued commentary, practical help, and steadfast support.

label: History
value: Davy Keith and Dora are twins.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were orphaned when their mother, Mary Keith, died after a long illness. Having no other immediate family available to care for them, they were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley at Green Gables. Davy quickly established himself as a handful, engaging in constant pranks such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck in church, trapping his sister in a toolhouse, putting a toad in Marilla's bed, and stealing plum jam. Under Anne's sympathetic and patient guidance, Davy gradually learned to distinguish right from wrong, promising never to tell falsehoods and working to improve his behavior. When his uncle Richard Keith passed away, leaving a trust fund for the twins, Marilla and Anne became his permanent guardians. Davy entered Avonlea School, formed a close friendship with Milty Boulter, and developed a keen interest in farming. Though he still engaged in occasional mischief, he grew into a reliable, hard-working boy who took pride in helping around Green Gables.

label: History
value: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley
unit: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley shortly after Anne arrives at Green Gables, and the two quickly swear eternal friendship at Orchard Slope. Throughout their childhood, Diana participates in Anne's games, imaginations, and the Avonlea Story Club. Despite a temporary separation imposed by her strict mother after accidentally drinking Marilla's currant wine, their bond remains unbroken, particularly after Anne saves Diana's little sister Minnie May during a bout of croup. Diana attends Avonlea School with Anne, though she does not pursue higher education at Queen's Academy or Redmond College. In her late teens, she becomes engaged to Fred Wright of Avonlea. They are married in a grand ceremony at Orchard Slope where Anne serves as her bridesmaid. Diana settles with Fred on a farm in Avonlea and gives birth to a son, Fred Jr., followed later by a daughter named Small Anne Cordelia.

label: Appearance
value: In his youth, Dick Moore was handsome.

After his departure on the Four Sisters, it was long believed that he had returned as a heavy, mentally impaired man with a thick beard. However, it was later revealed that the man who returned was actually his double and cousin, George Moore; the real Dick Moore had died years earlier in Cuba.

value: In his youth, Dick was selfish.

He was known to drink heavily, act carelessly, and pursue what he wanted relentlessly until he obtained it, only to lose interest afterward. He showed a tyrannical and domineering streak, leaving his young bride shortly after their forced marriage to go to sea.

label: History
value: Dick Moore grew up at Glen St. Mary
unit: Dick Moore grew up at Glen St. Mary as the son of storekeeper Abner Moore, working as a clerk in his father's shop in winter and going to sea in summer. Becoming infatuated with Leslie West, he pursued her despite her rejections, eventually forcing her into marriage at sixteen by threatening to foreclose the mortgage on her widowed mother's farm. Shortly after the marriage and the subsequent death of Leslie's mother, Dick left Four Winds on the ship Four Sisters bound for Cuba. For twelve years, the Four Winds community believed that Dick had been found in Havana by Captain Jim, suffering from brain trauma that left him a helpless, child-like invalid whom Leslie devotedly nursed. However, when Dr. Gilbert Blythe persuaded Leslie to send him to a Montreal hospital for an operation, the restored man was revealed to be Dick's cousin, George Moore. George disclosed that the real Dick Moore had actually contracted yellow fever and died in Cuba thirteen years prior to the surgery, before the Four Sisters ever sailed home.

label: History
value: Ellen West lived with Rosemary
unit: Ellen West lived for many years with her younger sister, Rosemary, in an old gray house on a hill overlooking Four Winds Harbor. In her youth, she had an affair with Norman Douglas, but after a sharp quarrel he abruptly married another woman. Following the death of their mother, a distraught Ellen coerced Rosemary into swearing on their mother's Bible that neither sister would ever marry or leave the other. Years later, when the widowed Rev. John Meredith proposed to Rosemary, Ellen adamantly refused to release her sister from her oath out of fear of being left alone. However, after Norman Douglas returned to her life and proposed to her, Ellen realized the injustice of her stance and offered to release Rosemary. When Rosemary initially refused to reopen the matter, Ellen declared she would not marry Norman if Rosemary remained alone. Eventually, after the Meredith children smoothed the way between their father and Rosemary, the sisters agreed to a double wedding, and Ellen married Norman Douglas in a September ceremony.

label: History
value: Faith Meredith moved to the Glen St. Mary manse
unit: Faith Meredith moved to the Glen St. Mary manse with her widowed father and siblings. Soon after arriving, she and her brothers and sister befriended the Blythe children in Rainbow Valley, as well as an escaped run-away named Mary Vance whom they found hiding in an old barn. After getting into various scrapes that scandalized the congregation, Faith helped establish a 'Good-Conduct Club' with her siblings to self-punish their misdeeds. Following a misunderstanding of days where she and Una cleaned the house on a Sunday, Faith took the pulpit platform in church the next Sabbath to publicly defend her father and explain their error. Later, when the congregation gossiped about her father, she marched to Norman Douglas's home to confront him; after an angry outburst, she won his friendship and convinced him to return to church. When Aunt Martha accidentally slaughtered her beloved pet rooster Adam to cook for a visiting minister, Faith was heartbroken, but was later comforted by Rosemary West, who gifted her a canary. Upon discovering that her father loved Rosemary, Faith privately approached her to clear up misunderstandings, ultimately paving the way for her father's marriage.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe grows up in Avonlea.
unit: Gilbert Blythe grows up in Avonlea and attends the local school, where he instantly sparks a long-standing rivalry with Anne Shirley after playfully calling her 'Carrots.' Though Anne refuses his apologies for years, Gilbert remains persistently fond of her whileexcelling academically. He attends Queen's Academy alongside Anne, where both graduate with top honors, after which he selflessly surrenders his appointment as the Avonlea schoolteacher so Anne can remain near Green Gables. He teaches at White Sands before attending Redmond College in Kingsport, graduating with High Honors in Classics and winning the prestigious Cooper Prize. Following his graduation, he studies medicine, completes his degree, and accepts a practice at Four Winds Harbor, succeeding his great-uncle, Dr. David Blythe. Gilbert marries Anne in the Green Gables orchard, and they settle in a small house on the harbor shore. Together they experience the grief of losing their firstborn infant daughter, Joyce, before welcoming their son, James Matthew ('Jem'). Later, Gilbert purchases the larger Morgan property in Glen St. Mary to accommodate his growing family and expanding medical practice.

He attends Queen's Academy alongside Anne, where both graduate with top honors, after which he selflessly surrenders his appointment as the Avonlea schoolteacher so Anne can remain near Green Gables. He teaches at White Sands before attending Redmond College in Kingsport, graduating with High Honors in Classics and winning the prestigious Cooper Prize. Following his graduation, he studies medicine, completes his degree, and accepts a practice at Four Winds Harbor, succeeding his great-uncle, Dr. David Blythe. Gilbert marries Anne in the Green Gables orchard, and they settle in a small house on the harbor shore. Together they experience the grief of losing their firstborn infant daughter, Joyce, before welcoming their son, James Matthew ('Jem'). Later, Gilbert purchases the larger Morgan property in Glen St. Mary to accommodate his growing family and expanding medical practice.

label: Personality
value: Mr. Harrison is considered an eccentric 'crank' by his Avonlea neighbors.
unit: Considered an eccentric 'crank' by his Avonlea neighbors, Mr. Harrison is very outspoken, hottempered, and prides himself on telling the blunt truth. Despite his crusty, crabbed, and quick-to-anger exterior, he has a kind heart, a warm sense of humor, and a genuine capacity for friendship. He is stubborn and cantankerous when provoked, but appreciates good company and admits his own flaws. Though previously known for sloppy bachelor housekeeping, he adapts to orderliness after reuniting with his wife.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea as one of Anne Shirley's primary classmates and friends. After studying at Queen's Academy, she earned a teacher's license with honors in domestic science. She taught school at Newbridge and later took a teaching position in western Canada. While in the West, she met and became engaged to Edward Inglis, a wealthy English Winnipeg millionaire. Returning to Avonlea, she was married in a grand ceremony at her home before moving to Winnipeg with her husband and later traveling to Europe on their honeymoon.

label: Personality
value: John Meredith is a deeply spiritual preacher.
unit: He is a deeply spiritual, learned, and eloquent preacher, but lacks practical common sense and is exceptionally absent-minded and moony. Though shy and aloof on the surface, he possesses the heart of a boy and a gentle, humble, and forgiving nature. He lives largely in a world of books and abstractions, often getting so absorbed in his reading or meditations that he forgets his meals and duties. He loves his children dearly, but struggles to manage them without a wife, ruling his home solely through love rather than sternness.

label: History
value: After the death of Cecilia, John Meredith was left alone to raise their four young children.
unit: After the death of his beloved wife, Cecilia, John Meredith was left alone to raise their four young children with the assistance of his elderly, half-blind relative, Aunt Martha. Moving from Maywater to Glen St. Mary, he accepted the call to become the minister of the Presbyterian church, winning the congregation over with his brilliant preaching despite his extreme absent-mindedness and the undisciplined antics of his motherless children. During his time at Glen St. Mary, he frequently lost himself in theological studies, forgetting meals, church announcements, and various pastoral duties. His children formed a 'Good-Conduct Club' to discipline themselves after public criticism of their behavior, leading to an incident where his daughter Una fainted from fasting, deeply shocking him into a realization of his parental shortcomings. Shortly after, Mrs. Alec Davis attempted to adopt Una, which he fiercely refused, declaring his love for his children. Over time, he developed deep feelings for Rosemary West, whom he met by a spring in Rainbow Valley, but when he proposed to her she rejected him by letter due to a secret vow she had made to her sister. Despairing of his love, he remained devoted to his family until Una, discovering his heartache and learning the truth from Rosemary, intervened to reconcile them. Re-assured of her affection, Mr. Meredith met Rosemary again at the spring, where she accepted his proposal, leading to their planned autumn marriage.

unit: After the death of his beloved wife, Cecilia, John Meredith was left alone to raise their four young children with the assistance of his elderly, half-blind relative, Aunt Martha. Moving from Maywater to Glen St. Mary, he accepted the call to become the minister of the Presbyterian church, winning the congregation over with his brilliant preaching despite his extreme absent-mindedness and the undisciplined antics of his motherless children. During his time at Glen St. Mary, he frequently lost himself in theological studies, forgetting meals, church announcements, and various pastoral duties. His children formed a 'Good-Conduct Club' to discipline themselves after public criticism of their behavior, leading to an incident where his daughter Una fainted from fasting, deeply shocking him into a realization of his parental shortcomings. Shortly after, Mrs. Alec Davis attempted to adopt Una, which he fiercely refused, declaring his love for his children. Over time, he developed deep feelings for Rosemary West, whom he met by a spring in Rainbow Valley, but when he proposed to her she rejected him by letter due to a secret vow she had made to her sister. Despairing of his love, he remained devoted to his family until Una, discovering his heartache and learning the truth from Rosemary, intervened to reconcile them. Re-assured of her affection, Mr. Meredith met Rosemary again at the spring, where she accepted his proposal, leading to their planned autumn marriage.

label: History
value: Josie Pye attended Avonlea School.
unit: Josie Pye attended Avonlea School, where she frequently clashed with Anne Shirley and other classmates. During her school years, she engaged in cheating during spelling lessons and dared Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, which resulted in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Later, Josie joined the Queen's Academy preparation class and studied at Queen's alongside Anne, Gilbert, and Jane Andrews. After graduating from Queen's, she attended Redmond College in Kingsport for higher education. Throughout her college years, Josie maintained a spiteful attitude towards Anne, making condescending remarks about Anne's background, writing, and romance, and falsely claiming Anne's prize-winning story was plagiarized. After completing her studies at Redmond, she planned to return for a second year.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis was engaged to Stephen Irving.
unit: In her youth, Lavendar Lewis was engaged to Stephen Irving, but after a silly quarrel and her own stubborn refusal to forgive him immediately, Stephen left for the United States, leaving her broken-hearted. She settled into a quiet, secluded life at Echo Lodge in Grafton, keeping up her spirits by imagining companion friends and hiring a series of young maidservants whom she called Charlotta. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon her home, discovering her setting a feast for imaginary guests, and they quickly became firm friends. Anne later introduced Stephen Irving's son, Paul, to Miss Lavendar, and eventually facilitated a reunion between Stephen and Miss Lavendar. The reunited lovers married under the honeysuckle arbor in her garden, after which they moved to Boston, returning to Echo Lodge to spend their summers.

label: Personality
value: Leslie was originally warm.
unit: Though originally warm, passionate, and vivid, years of tragedy and isolation made Leslie reserved, proud, and occasionally bitter. She harbors a fierce pride and an unyielding sense of duty, refusing to shirk any responsibility she has assumed. When freed from her tragic circumstances, her natural warmth, wit, and capacity for joy and deep love re-emerge.

label: History
value: Leslie Moore lived a tragic early life in Four Winds.
unit: Leslie Moore lived a tragic early life in Four Winds, marked by the horrific accidental death of her brother Kenneth and the suicide of her father. At sixteen, she sacrificed her ambitions of attending college to marry Dick Moore in order to prevent her mother from being turned out of her mortgaged home. Shortly after her mother's death, Dick went to sea and was reported lost. Years later, Captain Jim found him in a Havana hospital suffering from brain-trauma amnesia and brought him back. For twelve years, Leslie nursed the helpless man, taking in summer boarders to support them. When Anne Shirley moved to the Four Winds house of dreams, Leslie formed a deep friendship with her, though she initially struggled with feelings of envy over Anne's happy life. When Dr. Gilbert Blythe suggested an operation that might restore the man's memory, Leslie dutifully agreed to take him to a Montreal hospital. The operation proved that the man was actually Dick's cousin, George Moore; the real Dick Moore had died years earlier of yellow fever in Cuba. Realizing she was free, Leslie eventually confessed her love for writer Owen Ford, who had boarded with her that summer. The two became engaged and were later married, intending to spend their summers at Echo Lodge in Four Winds.

value: James Matthew Blythe was born in the house of dreams.

Soon after his birth, the family relocated to Ingleside in Glen St. Mary, where he grew up alongside his younger siblings and played frequently in Rainbow Valley. As he grew into a sturdy schoolboy, he developed a deep love for nature and outdoor adventures, becoming an expert fisherman and woodcrafter. At thirteen, after completing his early education at the Glen school, he left home to attend Queen's Academy in Charlottetown.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert and her brother Matthew intended to adopt an orphan boy.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert and her brother Matthew intended to adopt an orphan boy to help on their farm, but through a misunderstanding, Anne Shirley was sent to them instead. Though Marilla initially insisted on sending Anne back, she agreed to keep her upon seeing the child's plight and yielded to Matthew's quiet wishes. She took full charge of Anne's upbringing, attempting to curb her wild imagination, talkativeness, and temper with strict discipline, though she quickly grew deeply attached to her. Following Matthew's sudden death, Marilla faced the prospect of selling Green Gables due to failing eyesight, but Anne gave up her college scholarship to stay home and help her. Soon after, Marilla invited the widowed Mrs. Rachel Lynde to live at Green Gables, enabling Anne to attend Redmond College while the twins, Davy and Dora Keith, were brought to live at the homestead. Over the years, Marilla supported Anne through her college career, her engagement, and her marriage to Gilbert Blythe, eventually welcoming her grandchildren and continuing her life at Green Gables into advanced old age.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott grew up over-harbor
unit: Marshall Elliott grew up over-harbor in Four Winds. In his youth, he courted Ellen West for two years, but they broke off after a bitter quarrel; in a fit of pique, he married Hester Reese, who later died. During a heated general election fifteen years prior to the events of the late four-winds period, Marshall swore a public vow that he would not cut his hair or shave his beard until the Liberal party won power. True to his stubborn nature, he maintained this wild appearance for fifteen years, cultivating a river of brown beard and long hair that made him famous throughout the district. After the Liberals finally won the federal election, Marshall immediately went to the Glen village barber at midnight to be shaved and barbered. Clean-shaven and rejuvenated, he rekindled his courtship with Ellen West, whom he had loved all his life. After resolving her family complications and sister's broken vow, Ellen accepted his proposal, and the two were married in a double wedding alongside her sister Rosemary and John Meredith.

label: History
value: Mary Vance ran away from her abusive guardian
unit: Mary Vance ran away from her abusive guardian, Mrs. Wiley, after losing her saved money, and hid in James Taylor's old hay barn near Glen St. Mary. She was discovered starving by the Meredith children, who brought her secretly to the manse, fed her, and sheltered her in the garret. She quickly proved herself a capable helper, taking over household chores in the manse. When Mrs. Wiley suddenly died, Mary faced the prospect of being sent back to the Hopetown Orphan Asylum. Una Meredith, touched by Mary's fear of returning to the orphan asylum, begged Miss Cornelia Bryant to take her in. Miss Cornelia adopted Mary, bringing her into a comfortable home where she was well-clad and cared for. Mary quickly adapted to her new life, becoming a devoted helper to Miss Cornelia and a prominent, chatter-filled companion to the Meredith and Blythe children in Rainbow Valley.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert and Marilla decide to adopt an orphan boy.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert and his sister Marilla decide to adopt an orphan boy to help on their farm at Green Gables. Driving to Bright River station to collect the boy, Matthew instead finds Anne Shirley, an imaginative orphan girl sent by mistake. Too kind-hearted to leave her behind, he brings her to Green Gables and immediately takes a liking to her, quietly persuading Marilla to keep her. Over the years, Matthew becomes Anne's constant confidant and champion, encouraging her imaginative spirit and secretly buying her a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for Christmas. When Anne passes her college entrance exams with distinction, Matthew expresses his deep pride in her. Shortly after Anne finishes her studies at Queen's Academy, Matthew dies instantly from a heart attack caused by the shock of the Abbey Bank's failure, and is buried in the Avonlea graveyard.

label: History
value: In his youth, Norman Douglas courted Ellen West.
unit: In his youth, Norman Douglas courted Ellen West, but following a sudden quarrel he impulsively married Hester Reese, whom he survived. After a disagreement with his church over the burial of a dog, he refused to attend services for twenty years. Fifteen years before the Liberal political victory, he vowed never to shave or cut his hair until the Grits returned to power, earning a reputation for his eccentric appearance. When the election results finally favoured his party, he immediately went to a local barber to have his hair and beard trimmed. Prompted by seeing Ellen West again, he renewed his courtship and eventually convinced her to break a long-standing maiden vow, culminating in their marriage.

label: History
value: Owen Ford grew up knowing the lore of Four Winds Harbor.
unit: Owen Ford grew up knowing the lore of Four Winds Harbor from his mother, Alice Selwyn. After recovering from typhoid fever, he visited Four Winds in the summer to recuperate and search for inspiration for a novel. Staying at the Moore homestead as a boarder, he met Leslie Moore and quickly fell deeply in love with her, though he kept his feelings hidden due to her tragic marriage. During his stay, he struck up a close friendship with Captain Jim and collaborated with him to turn Captain Jim's 'life-book' into a manuscript. After concluding his work, he confessed his love for Leslie to Anne Blythe before departing. Later, upon the discovery that Leslie's husband was actually his cousin George Moore and that Leslie was free, Owen returned to Four Winds, declared his love, and became engaged to Leslie, planning to purchase the old house at Four Winds to serve as their summer home.

After concluding his work, he confessed his love for Leslie to Anne Blythe before departing. Later, upon the discovery that Leslie's husband was actually his cousin George Moore and that Leslie was free, Owen returned to Four Winds, declared his love, and became engaged to Leslie, planning to purchase the old house at Four Winds to serve as their summer home.

label: History
value: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea
unit: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea from the United States at age ten to live with his grandmother. He enters the Avonlea school under Anne Shirley, quickly forming a close bond with her as a kindred spirit. Throughout his schooldays, he populates his imagination with 'Rock People' and whimsical fairy-like creations. When his father, Stephen Irving, visits Avonlea, Paul helps reunite him with his former love, Miss Lavendar Lewis. Stephen and Miss Lavendar marry and eventually take Paul with them to live in Boston and later travel abroad. As he matures into a tall teenager, Paul develops his literary talent and begins writing published poetry, while maintaining an enduring affection for his former teacher.

During their Sophomore year, Phil joined Anne, Priscilla, and Stella Maynard in renting the cozy cottage known as Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue, where they lived with Aunt Jamesina. Though pursued by many suitors, Phil struggled to choose between her two home suitors, Alec and Alonzo, until she met Jonas Blake, a poor, devout theology student. Recognizing that she loved Jonas, she refused her former suitors and accepted Jonas's proposal despite her family's initial objections to his lack of wealth. She threw herself into household duties at Patty's Place, earned High Honors in Mathematics at graduation, and subsequently married Jonas to join him in his ministry in the city slums.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school, where he focused most of his efforts on preparing his advanced pupils for Queen's Academy while neglecting the younger children. During his tenure, he openly courted one of his older students, Prissy Andrews. He frequently disciplined pupils in a sarcastic manner, on one occasion making Anne Shirley stand in front of the blackboard with her name misspelled after she broke her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head. On another occasion, he forced Anne to sit with Gilbert Blythe as a punishment for arriving late, leading Anne to leave school for a period. At the end of the school term in June, he delivered an emotional farewell speech to his students before departing Avonlea. He was succeeded the following term by Miss Muriel Stacy.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Redmond College in Kingsport.
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Redmond College in Kingsport alongside Anne Shirley, Gilbert Blythe, and other friends from Prince Edward Island. During her time at Redmond, she lived at Patty's Place with Anne, Philippa Gordon, Stella Maynard, and Aunt Jamesina. Prior to entering Redmond, she taught school at Carmody for a time. At Redmond, Priscilla studied Classics, eventually graduating with Honors. Following her graduation, she travelled abroad to Japan, where she married a foreign missionary.

label: Personality
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a capable housewife
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a capable, notable housewife who prides herself on always speaking her mind without fear or favor. Highly outspoken, officious, and prone to gossiping, she manages her own concerns and those of her neighbors with equal vigor. Despite her brusque, opinionated manner and sharp tongue, she possesses a warm, kind heart and is always ready to help those in need or distress. She is a devout, staunch Conservative and Presbyterian who holds very firm, traditional views on social propriety and child-rearing.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow on the Avonlea main road
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived for decades in Lynde's Hollow on the Avonlea main road with her meek husband, Thomas. Active in all local affairs, she managed her household while running the Sewing Circle, helping with the Sunday School, and leading the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. When Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert adopted Anne Shirley, Rachel expressed loud disapproval and initially clashed with Anne over her blunt criticism of the girl's looks, though she quickly accepted Anne's apology and became one of her firmest supporters. Over the years, she offered endless advice on Anne's upbringing and community matters, regularly participating in church fundraisers and political rallies. Following a prolonged illness, Thomas Lynde passed away, leaving the farm mortgaged. Facing the necessity of selling her homestead, Rachel was invited by Marilla Cuthbert to move into Green Gables. She set up her own quarters in the former spare room and helped Marilla manage the household and the Keith twins, allowing Anne to leave for college at Redmond.

label: History
value: Jonas Blake attended Redmond College
unit: Jonas Blake attended Redmond College and St. Columbia to train for the ministry. While managing the Point Prospect Mission Church during a summer break, he met Philippa Gordon, who nicknamed him 'Jo.' Although she initially found his appearance unconventional, his sincerity, preaching talent, and warm disposition won her affection. Jonas hesitated to propose due to his poor financial prospects, but they eventually became engaged and were married the June following his graduation. After their wedding and a honeymoon in the land of Evangeline, the couple settled on Patterson Street, where Jo took charge of a slum mission church. He later attended the wedding of Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe, where he offered the wedding prayer.

label: History
value: Rilla Blythe is the youngest child of Dr. Gilbert Blythe
unit: Rilla Blythe is the youngest child of Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne Shirley, growing up at Ingleside in Glen St. Mary. During the summer when she was six years old, Susan Baker dressed her in fine clothes to carry a basket of fresh strawberries to the manse as a gift for Mr. Meredith. At the manse gate, she encountered Mary Vance, who tried to take the basket from her. When Rilla refused to give it up, Mary chased her down the Glen street while brandishing a large dried codfish. Terrified, Rilla fled until she stumbled into a mud puddle, ruining her finest dress, slippers, and hat, while dropping the strawberries. Miss Cornelia rescued her and took her home, where Susan Baker cleaned her up and comforted her.

During the summer when she was six years old, Susan Baker dressed her in fine clothes to carry a basket of fresh strawberries to the manse as a gift for Mr. Meredith. At the manse gate, she encountered Mary Vance, who tried to take the basket from her. When Rilla refused to give it up, Mary chased her down the Glen street while brandishing a large dried codfish. Terrified, Rilla fled until she stumbled into a mud puddle, ruining her finest dress, slippers, and hat, while dropping the strawberries. Miss Cornelia rescued her and took her home, where Susan Baker cleaned her up and comforted her.

label: History
value: Rosemary West grew up in a house.
unit: Rosemary West grew up in a secluded, vine-hung gray house on a hill near Glen St. Mary with her sister Ellen. At seventeen, her first love, Martin Crawford, was lost at sea, an event that deeply shadowed her early youth. Following the death of their mother, a distraught Ellen coerced Rosemary into swearing a solemn oath on the Bible that neither sister would ever marry or abandon the other. Rosemary lived quietly at the hill farm for years, teaching music to local children, including the Blythe twins. She met the widowed Presbyterian minister, John Knox Meredith, at the hidden spring in Rainbow Valley, where they formed a deep mutual attraction. When John eventually proposed to her, Rosemary—bound by her vow to Ellen—refused him by letter, leaving both heartbroken. Shortly afterwards, Norman Douglas renewed his courtship of Ellen, who agreed to marry him provided she released Rosemary from her oath. Rosemary then accepted John Meredith's proposal after his daughter, Una, visited her to ask if she would marry her father. Their double wedding with Ellen and Norman was planned for September, bringing joy and a long-awaited motherly presence to the motherless children of the manse.

label: History
value: Royal Gardner was born in Kingsport.
unit: Royal Gardner was born in Kingsport to a wealthy and aristocratic family. After completing his Freshman and Sophomore years at Redmond College, he was forced to pause his studies to accompany his ill mother to Europe for two years. Upon returning to Redmond to finish his Arts degree, he met Anne Shirley in the park during a heavy November rainstorm, rescuing her with his umbrella. He fell deeply in love with Anne, courting her over the next two years with flowers, poetry, and dedicated attentions, causing college circles to assume they would marry. In their Senior year, he brought his mother and sisters to meet Anne at Patty's Place. At the end of their college career, Roy proposed to Anne in the park pavilion where they had first met, but she unexpectedly rejected his proposal upon realizing she did not truly love him. A year later, Roy married another girl and subsequently achieved great literary success by writing a famous novel based on Captain Jim Boyd's life-book, which he composed while spending a summer at Four Winds Harbor.

label: History
value: Ruby grows up in Avonlea.
unit: Ruby grows up in Avonlea and attends the local school alongside Anne Shirley and Diana Barry. She later studies at Queen's Academy to become a teacher, participating in school recitations, concerts, and the Avonlea Story Club. After graduating from Queen's, she secures a teaching position at Carmody and later at White Sands. During her young adulthood, she enjoys an active social life, surrounded by numerous suitors, including Herb Spencer. However, after contracting a severe congestion in the winter, she develops galloping consumption and is forced to give up teaching. Throughout the following summer, she remains in denial about her failing health, continuing to talk gaily of her clothes and lovers. Shortly before her death, she finally admits her terminal illness and her deep fear of dying to Anne Shirley during a quiet evening in her garden. Ruby reconciles with her old friend Em White, makes peace with her fate, and passes away peacefully in her sleep at the end of the summer.

During her young adulthood, she enjoys an active social life, surrounded by numerous suitors, including Herb Spencer. However, after contracting a severe congestion in the winter, she develops galloping consumption and is forced to give up teaching. Throughout the following summer, she remains in denial about her failing health, continuing to talk gaily of her clothes and lovers. Shortly before her death, she finally admits her terminal illness and her deep fear of dying to Anne Shirley during a quiet evening in her garden. Ruby reconciles with her old friend Em White, makes peace with her fate, and passes away peacefully in her sleep at the end of the summer.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy is hired as the new teacher for Avonlea School.
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy is hired as the new teacher for Avonlea School, succeeding Mr. Phillips as the first female teacher in the village's history. She quickly wins the hearts of her pupils by introducing interactive teaching methods, physical culture exercises, nature field days, and Friday recitation afternoons. In November of her first year, she organizes a successful student concert to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag. Later, she forms an advanced class for students preparing for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations. Although offered a position in her home district's grade school, she decides to remain in Avonlea to see her entrance class through to their exams. Under her guidance and drilling, all of her candidates successfully pass their Queen's entrance examinations at the end of the term.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, completing her third year before taking up a career as a country schoolteacher. Finding the repetitive complaints of parents, the multi-grade duties, and the loneliness of boardinghouses tedious, she resolved to quit teaching and pursue a degree at Redmond College. She proposed renting a furnished house in Kingsport where she, Anne, Priscilla, and Philippa Gordon could live together, bringing her aunt, Jamesina, to act as housekeeper. During their time at Patty's Place, Stella managed the household accounts and participated in the social life and academic rivalries of Redmond, successfully completing her course work and graduating alongside her friends.

label: History
value: Susan Baker entered the service of Gilbert and Anne Blythe.
unit: Susan Baker originally entered the service of Gilbert and Anne Blythe as a maid-of-all-work at their first home, the 'house of dreams' near Four Winds Harbor. When Anne suffered from a prolonged illness following the birth of her son Shirley, Susan stepped in to nurse and hand-rear the infant, forming a lifelong maternal bond with him. She subsequently relocated with the family to their permanent home, Ingleside, in Glen St. Mary. Throughout the years, she managed the household with tireless energy, cooked indefatigably for the family, and stoutly defended the Blythe children and Mr. Meredith's neglected family against local gossip. During an absence when she went to care for her sister Matilda, who had broken her leg, she temporarily yielded her kitchen duties to Leslie Moore, but returned as soon as possible to resume her position as the undisputed helm of the Ingleside household.

Throughout the years, she managed the household with tireless energy, cooked indefatigably for the family, and stoutly defended the Blythe children and Mr. Meredith's neglected family against local gossip. During an absence when she went to care for her sister Matilda, who had broken her leg, she temporarily yielded her kitchen duties to Leslie Moore, but returned as soon as possible to resume her position as the undisputed helm of the Ingleside household.

value: Una is a gentle child.
unit: Una is a gentle, sensitive, and deeply empathetic child who cares intensely about the well-being of her family. She is shy, timid, and easily frightened by ghosts or conflict, yet she possesses a quiet, heroic courage when those she loves are hurting. Thoughtful and devout, she takes great comfort in prayer and spiritual things, longing for a peaceful, orderly life. Unlike her more daring siblings, Una hates fisticuffs and strife, desiring only to stay at home and surround her loved ones with affection.

label: History
value: Una Meredith grew up in the Maywater manse.
unit: Una Meredith grew up in the Maywater manse until the age of ten, when her father accepted a call to Glen St. Mary. Following her mother's early death, Una and her siblings lived under the haphazard care of her father and their elderly relative, Aunt Martha, leading a neglected, wild existence. Shortly after arriving in the Glen, Una and her siblings discovered Mary Vance, a runaway orphan, hiding in a barn, and helped shelter her at the manse. After Mary's terrifying tales about cruel stepmothers, Una became secretly terrified that her father would remarry. When she discovered her father's deep sorrow over a failed romance, Una heroically conquered her own fears and visited Rosemary West, begging her to marry her father to make him happy. Her selfless plea touched Rosemary, resolving the misunderstanding between the adults and paving the way for their marriage. Una also participated in the Good-Conduct Club formed with her siblings to discipline themselves, once fasting until she fainted in church. She subsequently found deep happiness in the family's union with Rosemary West.

unit: Una Meredith grew up in the Maywater manse until the age of ten, when her father accepted a call to Glen St. Mary. Following her mother's early death, Una and her siblings lived under the haphazard care of her father and their elderly relative, Aunt Martha, leading a neglected, wild existence. Shortly after arriving in the Glen, Una and her siblings discovered Mary Vance, a runaway orphan, hiding in a barn, and helped shelter her at the manse. After Mary's terrifying tales about cruel stepmothers, Una became secretly terrified that her father would remarry. When she discovered her father's deep sorrow over a failed romance, Una heroically conquered her own fears and visited Rosemary West, begging her to marry her father to make him happy. Her selfless plea touched Rosemary, resolving the misunderstanding between the adults and paving the way for their marriage. Una also participated in the Good-Conduct Club formed with her siblings to discipline themselves, once fasting until she fainted in church. She subsequently found deep happiness in the family's union with Rosemary West.

label: Quotes
value: > How the air shines to-night. The flower angel has been walking over the world to-day, calling to the flowers. I can see his blue wings on that hill by the woods.

label: Quotes
value: > Some day the Pied Piper will come over the hill up there and down Rainbow Valley, piping merrily and sweetly. And I will follow him—follow him down to the shore—down to the sea—away from you all. I don't think I'll want to go—Jem will want to go—it will be such an adventure—but I won't. Only I'll have to—the music will call and call and call me until I must follow.

label: Quotes
value: > I didn't say I would run. I said I wanted to run. That's a different thing. I want to help people, too. But oh, I wish there weren't any ugly, dreadful things in the world. I wish everything was glad and beautiful.

label: Quotes
value: > I never fought before—and I didn't want to right up to the last—and then I liked it while I was at it.

label: Quotes
value: > I'm not going to be frightened any more, sir. Being frightened of things is worse than the things themselves.

label: History
value: Walter grew up at Ingleside
unit: Walter grew up at Ingleside in Glen St. Mary, spending his leisure time exploring the nearby woods and Rainbow Valley with his brothers, sisters, and the Meredith children from the manse. Often considered 'girly' by schoolmates because he preferred reading poetry to fighting or participating in rough sports, Walter nevertheless commanded a quiet respect for his eloquence and storytelling ability. During a summer evening in Rainbow Valley, he introduced the myth of the Pied Piper to his companions, experiencing a chilling premonition that he and the other boys would one day be called away to follow a distant piper. When Dan Reese insulted his mother's writings and called Faith Meredith names, Walter overcame his deep-seated dread of violence and challenged Dan to a fight. Despite agonizing over the upcoming fistfight for an entire night, Walter stood his ground, fought fiercely, and defeated Dan, earning a newfound confidence and the respect of those around him. He later made peace with his fears by voluntarily going to the dentist to have a troublesome tooth extracted.
